_comment: Mesh repo-templating token classifier (Phase 1 pilot). Consumed by render-handlebars.js and referenced by scripts/secret-scan.sh. sed remains the DEFAULT renderer; this governs the opt-in Handlebars path and future repo emission.

allowlist._comment: Git-safe brand-delta tokens that MAY be substituted into an emitted repo. These are tenant-brand OR per-repo code identity, never secrets. BRAND/BRAND_TITLE/CLUSTER_DOMAIN/HARBOR_PROJECT are live in templates/apps. HOST_NAME/NPM_SCOPE were PROMOTED reserved_pilot -> live in Phase 4 (the angular-mfe archetype federation-base.js + package.json recipe consume them). GENERATOR_ORG_GROUP is the CI-include org/group (all archetype recipes). ORG_SLUG (registered live like NPM_SCOPE) is the SAME ORG lowercased slug exposed as a PATH-SAFE FILENAME token — the generator archetype's renames[] demo (docs/BRANDING-{{ORG_SLUG}}.md) consumes it; derived in render-repo-tree.sh from the single slug rule, never operator-supplied. Phase-4 reserved_pilot = per-repo IDENTITY tokens carried by the repos[] manifest, NOT brand: APP_SLUG (angular-mfe npm segment / ng target / <snap-SLUG-root>), TITLE_WORD (per-UI tab-title differentiator), PROFILE (gateway be|fe|pki deploy profile). All ORG/BRAND/repo-derived, none secret-bearing. MFA_ENABLED (issue #47) is the per-domain gateway MFA flip rendered into the tenant gateway Applications' mfa.enabled — a CLOSED two-value 'true'/'false' derived from the brand profile's MFA knob by both engines (never free text, never a secret). CASDOOR_ORG (issue #47, Domain.idp=own) is the Casdoor organization of an own-IdP brand's realm — a DNS-label-validated slug (default: the BRAND slug; on a mesh node synthesised from the #118 DomainEntry.casdoorOrg), consumed by templates/apps/05-casdoor.yaml.hbs + templates/manifests/casdoor/*, which render ONLY for IDP=own profiles.

denylist._comment: Secret-bearing keys derived from brands/example.conf + brand.conf.example. Rendering/emit MUST refuse to substitute or emit any of these. Exact keys plus a catch-all regex over key NAMES.

frozen_protocol_constants._comment: OUT-OF-SCOPE-FOR-TOKENIZATION. These are wire/label protocol identity, NOT tenant brand. They must stay literal in every emitted repo and must NEVER be turned into {{tokens}} nor rewritten by any renderer. A blind reverse-substitution that rebrands the literal 'hugmesh' would corrupt these. ENFORCED (fail-closed) by token-classifier.isFrozen(): render-handlebars.js refuses any requested/referenced token that lands on one of these — the Phase-3 red-team gate (a brand profile that tries to override e.g. hugmesh.net/domain is BLOCKED at emit, exit 1). The SAME set is what every build-*-stage4.sh rebrand_sysroot() sed chain protects behind sentinels in the baked device tree (tests/scripts/test-rebrand-frozen-label-keys.sh): label KEYS `hugmesh.net/<suffix>` in every structural-boundary shape (incl. KEY=VALUE and the escaped-dot jsonpath spelling), and the api_groups below in every spelling (apiVersion, apiGroups, ArgoCD group, the CRD's own name). api_groups: the k8s CRD API group is compiled into hugmesh-admin-bff-api (Fabric8 .withGroup("platform.hugmesh.net")) exactly like a label key is compiled into an operator — a fork that rebrands the CRD manifests but not the JVM 404s every OptionalService call. `<sub>.hugmesh.net` as a HOST (id., registry., admin., …) is NOT frozen and rebrands to <sub>.<CLUSTER_DOMAIN>.

theme_contract_constants._comment: THE CROSS-PROCESS THEME CONTRACT — the fleet's most fragile hand-off, and (unlike hugmesh-deploy.yaml) one that NOTHING guarded until this block existed. The theme text is derived in ONE place (Studio core/theme.py, mirrored by scripts/tooling/derive-theme.py) and then crosses FIVE process boundaries by NAME ALONE, with no schema, no version and no handshake: (0) an operator's derived theme persists to tests/stack/.theme.css, which the Makefile picks up by a `wildcard` on that EXACT path (STACK_THEME_FILE, line ~1529) — rename the file and the wildcard just misses, STACK_THEME_ENV expands to nothing, and every subsequent terminal `make stack-up` silently reverts to the shipped brand with no warning and no error; (1) the derived css text is handed to a container as an env var whose NAME is half the contract. As of the 2026-08-20 producer flip that name is HUG_THEME_CSS and the pre-rebrand SNAP_THEME_CSS is its LEGACY twin, and BOTH stay pinned here for the same LEGACY_COMPAT reason --sd-* does: the old spelling is still read by every 50-snap-theme.sh in the fleet and still accepted by compose's `${HUG_THEME_CSS:-${SNAP_THEME_CSS:-}}` value, so templating it breaks the hand-off exactly as loudly (which is to say, not at all) as templating the live one. Concretely: compose.local.yaml declares HUG_THEME_CSS on all 13 themed services; the Makefile's STACK_THEME_ENV threads the operator's stack-theme file back in under that name; the Studio's LocalStackNode._build_env exports BOTH (it is the one producer that can version-skew from the checkout it drives); on the cluster the name is the ConfigMap DATA KEY that specs/cluster/manifests/social-ui/deployment.yaml reads via valueFrom.configMapKeyRef.key, where derive-theme.py emits only the new key and the Deployment declares an optional ref for EACH so a ConfigMap of either vintage resolves; (2) the login-ui image's docker-entrypoint.d hook 50-snap-theme.sh DUAL-READS, preferring $HUG_THEME_CSS and falling back to $SNAP_THEME_CSS, at container START — that dual read shipped to all 13 consumer images BEFORE the producers moved, which is the only sequencing under which this rename is not a silent outage; (3) the hook writes the text to snap-theme.css (SNAP_THEME_OUT names its path inside the image, because the docroot is not writable for uid 101); (4) every UI's index.html <link rel=stylesheet href="snap-theme.css"> — and the Studio's login/platform preview asset's <style id="snap-theme"> marker — pull that exact filename; (5) the css body itself only takes effect because the UIs read the SAME custom property names the derived text declares — a shell's :root themes the remotes it federates, because a remote mounts inside the shell's document and its own global stylesheet is never loaded, so the prefix is a genuine CROSS-REPO contract and not one repo's private convention. TWO prefixes are live and BOTH are pinned: --hug-* is the current one (measured in this tree on 2026-08-20: 3119 reads in the built fleet remotes under tests/stack/.uidist/_remotes vs 9 for --sd-*; hugmesh-login-ui, the angular-mfe archetype's own exemplar, defines its :root under it), and --sd-* is the RETIRED spelling that the angular-host/angular-mfe skeletons still scaffolded new repos onto until PR #104 moved them — same LEGACY_COMPAT reasoning: a spelling still read anywhere in the fleet breaks identically to the live one when it is swept, so it stays pinned until nothing can carry it. Pinning ONLY --sd-* would have guarded 9 reads and left 3119 open, which is why the count is recorded here rather than assumed. SNAP_WEB_LOCALES rides the identical shape: Makefile var -> compose build arg -> the login-ui Dockerfile's ARG. Rename ANY link in that chain on ONE side and the whole chain still builds, still boots, still exits 0 — it just serves an unthemed page, which is precisely the failure mode a mechanical rebrand sweep produces and no test catches. So the names are pinned here BEFORE anyone sweeps. ENFORCED, not documentation: `rename_denylist` is collected by token-classifier.isRenameContractFile() — which sweeps EVERY top-level block here for a `rename_denylist` array, so a future contract family is a tokens.json edit with no code change — and unioned into render-recipe.js's renames[] contract guard (a recipe naming one of these files on EITHER side aborts the whole render, exit 1, same fail-closed shape as the deploy-descriptor/provenance names). Those descriptor names stay LITERAL in render-recipe.js and are NOT moved here: scripts/validate-catalog-discovery.sh static-parses that Set with a regex to prove every catalog-accepted descriptor is rename-protected, and a name it cannot evaluate would make the gate's view of the Set silently disagree with the engine's. Note these are PATHS, not {{tokens}} — a filename must never be added to denylist.keys instead, because scripts/secret-scan.sh mirrors that list and would raise a false secret finding. `env_keys` + `css_variable_prefixes` are matched by token-classifier.isThemeContract() inside render-handlebars.assertTemplateSafe(), so a template or recipe anchor that tries to TOKENIZE one is refused at emit — including the raw-mustache form {{--sd-accent}}, which is not a Handlebars identifier and therefore used to slip both reference-side loops and render to an EMPTY string, silently deleting the custom property it named. Behavioural coverage: tests/domain-registry/test-templating-rename-pr.sh cases A9e-A9m — those also assert the WIRING, not just the entries: if the union ever stops being evaluated or this block is renamed, the engine's Set silently shrinks back to the literal descriptor names and nothing else in the tree would notice, because the catalog-discovery gate only static-parses the literal half. TO LIFT: the sequenced migration (rename BOTH sides of a link in the same change, image + consumer) deletes the one line naming it here — that deliberate one-line edit is the whole point of pinning it.
